stories.title: Lee & Associates Negotiates Land Sale for Planned Industrial Development
stories.excerpt: Lee & Associates has closed a $4.5 million sale transaction for four acres located at 11330 W. Melrose Avenue in Franklin Park, Illinois. Jeff Provenza, principal at Lee & Associates’ Illinois office, represented the buyer, Seefried Industrial Properties. Provenza and his team have also been retained for leasing. The seller was O’Brien Investment Group. “This prime-infill location in the O’Hare Submarket benefits from I-294 frontage and visibility and a strong labor force,” said Provenza. “With 32’ ceilings and 14 exterior loading docks, this building will serve as a great new home for any company looking to operate in one of the strongest submarkets in the Chicagoland area.” The proposed industrial development will feature 81,687 square feet of state-of-the-art industrial space. The project is expected to be delivered in the second quarter of 2027. The post Lee & Associates Negotiates Land Sale for Planned Industrial Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Seefried Industrial acquired 4 acres in Franklin Park, IL O'Hare submarket for $4.5M
81,687 sq ft state-of-the-art industrial facility delivers Q2 2027
I-294 frontage and 32' ceilings designed for logistics/distribution tenants
stories.summary: Lee & Associates brokered a $4.5 million land sale to Seefried Industrial Properties in Franklin Park, Illinois (O'Hare submarket), a four-acre infill site with I-294 visibility. The buyer plans an 81,687-square-foot industrial development with 32-foot ceilings and 14 loading docks, targeting delivery in Q2 2027. The location emphasizes strong labor access and prime positioning for logistics operators.
stories.impact: Industrial demand in Chicago's O'Hare submarket remains robust, signaling sustained logistics/e-commerce activity that will compete with labor and infrastructure resources. Multifamily developers should monitor labor cost inflation and pipeline saturation in nearby residential submarkets (Franklin Park, Des Plaines) as industrial growth absorbs local workforce and drives potential housing demand.

stories.title: Wentworth Tech Breaks Ground on Residence Tower for First-Year Students
stories.excerpt: Wentworth Institute of Technology has broken ground on the First-Year Tower, an 18-story, 240,450-square-foot residence hall that will house 972 students and bring the Boston university’s entire first-year residential class together in a single building for the first time. The $200-million project is the largest capital undertaking in Wentworth’s history. Designed to meet Passive House standards and fully electrified, it will be among the first residence halls of its kind in Massachusetts. The building is scheduled to open to residents in August 2028. “We deliberately made the decision to dedicate this building to our first-year students,” said Wentworth president Mark A. Thompson. “The first year sets everything in motion. It is a transformational time when students find themselves, discover what they are capable of, and start to see what is possible for the future. Everything that follows, from co-ops to capstones to earning a degree, grows out of what happens in that first year.” The post Wentworth Tech Breaks Ground on Residence Tower for First-Year Students appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wentworth Institute broke ground on 18-story, 972-bed student residence hall
$200M project (largest in institution's history) opens August 2028
Passive House certified, fully electrified—signals ESG/cost-of-operations driver for institutional housing
stories.summary: Wentworth Institute of Technology has begun construction on a $200 million, 240,450-square-foot residence tower housing 972 first-year students, scheduled to open August 2028. The 18-story building is designed to Passive House standards and fully electrified, making it among the first residence halls of its kind in Massachusetts. The project consolidates the entire first-year class into a single building.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, the $200M capital deployment signals strong institutional housing investment confidence in Boston, which could raise construction cost expectations and labor competition for nearby residential projects; monitor for cost inflation bleed-over into private multifamily development in the Boston metro.

stories.title: Two AI Companies Ink Full-Floor Deals at 61 West 23rd Street
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence firms Normal Computing and Inspiren have inked full-floor office leases at 61 West 23rd Street in Manhattan’s Flatiron District. The two deals total 16,734 square feet at the Zegna family- and Taconic Partners-owned building between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas, according to landlord broker Cushman & Wakefield. C&W’s Connor Daugstrup represented the landlord in both deals alongside Taconic Development Advisors’ George Tsapelas. Normal Computing, which develops AI hardware, took 8,367 square feet at the seven-story building in a relocation and expansion of its New York City headquarters. The company currently occupies 5,250 square feet three blocks south at 27 West 20th Street, a spokesperson for Normal Computing told Commercial Observer, and plans to move to its new home in November. The spokesperson noted that approximately 30 employees will operate from Normal Computing’s new headquarters, with sufficient space to support plans to double its New York headcount over the coming year. Savills’ Gabe Marans and Maxine Rosen negotiated the headquarters lease on behalf of Normal Computing. The other high-tech arrival at 61 West 23rd Street, Inspiren, provides an AI-powered technology platform for senior living communities. Inspiren moved into its 8,367-square-foot space in early September, a company spokesperson told CO, marking its first permanent office in New York City. Previous records place Inspiren’s New York City operations at 19 Morris Avenue in Brooklyn’s Navy Yard. Inspiren was represented by Newmark’s Adam Spector and Ally Krieger. The Zegna family and Taconic acquired 61 West 23rd Street for $65 million in 2016. Taconic was tapped to reposition the building, restoring its historic façade and repositioning its interiors with two new lobbies, modernized elevators and pre-built offices. bullets: AI firms Normal Computing and Inspiren leased 16,734 sq ft at 61 West 23rd St, Manhattan
Normal Computing expanding from 5,250 to 8,367 sq ft, doubling NYC headcount target
Office leasing activity in Flatiron signals tech talent retention and NYC HQ expansion post-pandemic
stories.summary: AI-focused companies Normal Computing (hardware) and Inspiren have signed full-floor leases totaling 16,734 square feet at Taconic Partners' 61 West 23rd Street in Manhattan's Flatiron District. Normal Computing is relocating and expanding from a smaller footprint three blocks south, planning to grow its New York headcount from ~30 to 60 employees. Both leases reflect continued office demand from high-growth tech firms.
stories.impact: Office leasing rebounds for AI-sector tenants may increase near-term competition for skilled workers in Manhattan, supporting demand for high-amenity rental housing in walkable neighborhoods (Flatiron, NoMad, East Village). Monitor absorption and rent growth in proximate multifamily submarkets; strong office-tenant growth can drive affluent renter influx and support stabilized/value-add acquisition targets.

stories.title: 309-Unit Waterfront Community in Madison Celebrates Grand Opening
stories.excerpt: Clarion Partners, Vermilion Development, and Quartz Lake Capital recently hosted a ribbon-cutting event at the newly opened multifamily community, The Duncan, at 1625 Lock Lane in Madison, Wisconsin. Located on approximately 8.2 acres along Madison’s Isthmus, the 309-unit property offers lakeside living with proximity to downtown Madison. The Duncan includes studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences, as well as townhome options. The development brought together Vermilion Development, Clarion Partners, and Quartz Lake Capital as equity partners and CIBC as the lender. Potter Lawson served as the architect, and McShane Construction Company was the general contractor. JLL sourced the project’s equity and debt, and Greystar serves as the property manager. “Our mission at Vermilion is to create spaces that enrich people’s lives, and The Duncan was designed specifically for Madison — connected to the lake, Tenney Park, trails, bikes and downtown,” said Dave Cocagne, President and CEO of Vermilion Development. The post 309-Unit Waterfront Community in Madison Celebrates Grand Opening appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Duncan, 309-unit lakefront community in Madison, WI grand opened at 1625 Lock Lane
Mixed-unit (studios to 3-bed, townhomes) on 8.2 acres with Greystar management
Clarion Partners, Vermilion Development, Quartz Lake Capital partnership; CIBC debt financing
stories.summary: Clarion Partners, Vermilion Development, and Quartz Lake Capital celebrated the opening of The Duncan, a 309-unit multifamily community on 8.2 lakefront acres in Madison, Wisconsin. The property offers studios through three-bedroom units and townhomes, with proximity to downtown, Tenney Park, and biking infrastructure. CIBC provided debt financing, with Greystar managing operations.
stories.impact: Successful completion and stabilization of premium waterfront product in Madison signals steady rental demand and institutional capital confidence in secondary Wisconsin markets. For developers, this validates Madison's absorption capacity and willingness to pay for location-plus-amenity positioning; monitor Class A rent growth post-stabilization to gauge feasibility of new competing projects in the submarket.

stories.title: Belmont Park Reopens for Racing After $555M Reconstruction
stories.excerpt: New York Gov. Katy Hochul on Sunday cut the ribbon to mark the reopening of Belmont Park on Long Island after three years and $555 million of modernization. In addition to the return of the Belmont Stakes and the Breeders Cup in 2027, the facility will host year-round racing for the first time in its history. Along with putting up a new five-story grandstand five-story grandstand, the New York Racing Association (NYRA) has also modernized the racing and training facilities at Belmont Park by constructing four new racetracks, including the traditional 1 1/2-mile dirt track, two turf courses and a one-mile Tapeta oval. The reconstruction of Belmont Park was made possible by a $455- million state loan. When fully complete, the new Belmont Park will ultimately have a capacity of at least 50,000 spectators for the Belmont Stakes and major racing events, matching the capacity of the historic Saratoga Race Course, according to Hochul’s office. The post Belmont Park Reopens for Racing After $555M Reconstruction appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Belmont Park reopened after $555M, 3-year reconstruction on Long Island
New 5-story grandstand, four new racetracks, 50,000+ spectator capacity
$455M state loan financed modernization; year-round racing new to venue
stories.summary: New York Governor Katy Hochul cut the ribbon on Belmont Park after $555 million and three years of modernization funded largely by a $455 million state loan. The facility now features a new five-story grandstand, four racetracks (1.5-mile dirt, two turf, one Tapeta), and will operate year-round racing for the first time. Capacity reaches 50,000 spectators for major events.
stories.impact: Minor relevance to multifamily development. However, the significant state capital allocation and job creation (year-round operations, construction, hospitality) in Long Island may marginally support rental demand in nearby Gateway communities (Elmont, Queens border areas). Monitor for any spillover employment or visitor-economy housing demand, but impact is unlikely to move needle on multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: Investor Pays $15M For Nebraska Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Dakota Pointe, a 143-unit multifamily property in the south end of South Sioux City, Nebraska, sold for $15.3 million, or approximately $107,000 per unit. Greysteel represented the seller. Both the buyer and the seller are private investors based in South Dakota. The property drew multiple offers, and the closing structure met the seller’s timing requirements and the buyer’s long-term hold objectives. At closing, Dakota Pointe was fully occupied and featured a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units in a property built in 1994. “Buyers are looking harder at Midwest secondary markets than they were a year ago, and Dakota Pointe drew that interest quickly,” said Ryan Carter, Senior Director, Investment Sales at Greysteel. “The investors we surveyed at mid-year told us steady rental demand and yield drive their buying in markets like this one, and Dakota Pointe delivers both.” Greysteel covers Nebraska, Iowa and surrounding states from its Omaha and West Des Moines offices. The post Investor Pays $15M For Nebraska Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dakota Pointe, 143-unit apt in South Sioux City, NE sold for $15.3M ($107K/unit)
Both buyer and seller are South Dakota-based private investors; property fully occupied
Greysteel notes Midwest secondary markets seeing renewed buyer interest driven by yield
stories.summary: Dakota Pointe, a 143-unit multifamily property in South Sioux City, Nebraska, sold for $15.3 million ($107,000 per unit) to a South Dakota-based private investor. Built in 1994, the property was fully occupied at close with a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units. The sale attracted multiple offers and reflects growing investor appetite for Midwest secondary markets.
stories.impact: Midwest secondary markets (Nebraska, Iowa, South Dakota) showing renewed capital influx and sustained rental demand/yield fundamentals. At $107K/unit, cap rates likely attractive relative to coastal markets; developers should monitor South Sioux City, Omaha, Des Moines pipelines for new-build feasibility. Steady rental demand and demographic stability in these regions support long-hold institutional acquisitions and potential development site activity.

bullets: Moody's Jeffrey Havsy discusses underpriced CRE risks beyond property fundamentals
Alternative data (tenant credit, crime, truck traffic) and climate/robotics impact valuations
Cap rate reliance criticized; emphasis on location scores, hidden industrial asset risks
stories.summary: In a Moody's Analytics podcast, Jeffrey Havsy (CRE industry practice lead) explores risks investors are missing in commercial real estate underwriting. Key themes include over-reliance on cap rates, importance of alternative data (tenant credit, crime metrics, truck traffic), climate and robotics disruption to asset valuation, and the limitations of traditional property-level analysis. Havsy emphasizes the need for broader economic and credit context.
stories.impact: Signals evolving underwriting standards and risk awareness in the debt/equity markets that will affect multifamily development feasibility and capital availability. Developers should expect lenders to scrutinize tenant-mix credit quality, submarket crime trends, and long-term labor/demographic resilience more closely; this will widen spreads and tighten leverage for higher-risk submarkets, advantaging prime locations and experienced sponsors with strong lease quality and workforce stability.

stories.title: Principal Asset Management Adds Drew Fung for Debt Role
stories.excerpt: Drew Fung, who led Clarion Partners’ commercial real estate debt investment group for the last 14 years, will be taking on a similar role at Principal Asset Management. Principal appointed Fung as managing director of portfolio management focusing on commercial real estate debt investing, with a big emphasis on high-yield and structured debt strategies, the company announced Monday. He will be based out of New York City and report to Chris Duey, senior managing director at Principal Asset Management. Fung has originated more than $3.5 billion across mezzanine and structured debt investments during his nearly 40-year career, according to Principal. He was an honoree on Commercial Observer’s Power Finance list with Clarion for three straight years from 2022 to 2024. Clarion Partners did not immediately return a request for comment. Prior to arriving at Clarion in 2012, Fung was a managing director at Deutsche Bank for six and a half years leading high-yield debt investments. He also held roles at CWCapital and Lendlease during a CRE finance career that dates back to 1987. Fung is also active at the CRE trade association level as a member of the CRE Finance Council (CREFC), the Mortgage Bankers Association and the Urban Land Institute. He also serves on the steering committee of the National Council of Real Estate Investment Fiduciaries/CREFC debt fund index launched in 2023. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Drew Fung departed Clarion Partners (14 years) to join Principal Asset Management
Fung leads debt portfolio management, focus on high-yield and structured debt strategies
Career includes $3.5B originated across mezzanine and structured debt; 40-year CRE background
stories.summary: Drew Fung, who spent 14 years leading Clarion Partners' commercial real estate debt investment group, has joined Principal Asset Management as managing director of portfolio management. Fung will oversee commercial real estate debt investing with emphasis on high-yield and structured debt strategies from NYC. Over a 40-year career, he has originated more than $3.5 billion in mezzanine and structured debt.
stories.impact: Talent migration from traditional CRE platforms (Clarion) to insurance/asset managers (Principal) reflects capital reallocation and consolidation in debt markets. Developers should monitor Principal's asset class preferences and underwriting appetite post-Fung; his structured debt expertise suggests emphasis on complex recapitalizations and mezz strategies, which may widen cost of capital for standard bridge financing and increase reliance on construction lenders for stabilized development.

stories.title: Santander Bank, Washington Capital Provide $113M Debt for Chicago Office Conversion
stories.excerpt: Commonwealth Development Partners and Triangle Capital Group have secured $113 million to finance the conversion of an empty 25-story office building at 500 North Michigan Avenue into 384 mixed-income rental apartments in downtown Chicago. Santander Bank provided $71.5 million of non-recourse construction debt, while Washington Capital Management provided $41.5 million of joint venture equity. JLL Capital Markets’ Chris Knight, Ryan Planek and Annie Thomas arranged the transaction. Crain’s Chicago Business first reported the deal. As the building will retain its vintage 1960s-era architecture, the project aims to secure Federal Historic Tax Credits, while also securing tax benefits from the Illinois Affordable Housing Special Assessment Program. Washington Capital Management’s Robin Dean called the joint venture of Commonwealth Development Partners and Triangle Capital Group “an experienced sponsorship team,” and described 500 North Michigan Avenue as “an irreplaceable location and a thoughtful adaptive reuse strategy.” “We believe [the asset] is well positioned to meet long-term demand for high-quality housing in downtown Chicago,” she added. Commonwealth Development Partners and Triangle Capital Group acquired the vacant office building for only $5 million last August. In April, Washington Capital Management purchased 21,565 square feet of retail space connected to the ground floor of the building for $41 million from Commonwealth Development Partners. Located in the heart of the Chicago Loop along the famous “Magnificent Mile” in the city’s Streeterville neighborhood — which includes Northwestern Memorial Hospital, Lurie Children’s Hospital and the University of Chicago Booth School of Business — 500 North Michigan Avenue will deliver more than 250,000 square feet of rentable apartment space to the downtown area. stories.impact: Chicago's downtown office conversion pipeline is accelerating with strong debt + equity support, signaling capital availability for adaptive reuse and a strategy to absorb vacant Class A office stock. This transformation will increase multifamily supply in prime downtown Chicago submarkets and compress rents in adjacent neighborhoods; developers should assess competitive exposure in River North, West Loop, and Pilsen and adjust positioning toward higher-amenity/specialized (student, senior, luxury) submarkets or secondary locations.

stories.title: Related Group, Tricap Sell Casa Tua-Leased Retail Condo in Miami’s Wynwood
stories.excerpt: The Pérez family’s Related Group and David Edelstein’s Tricap have sold the newly completed ground-floor retail space at the NoMad Hotel-branded condo development in Miami for $33 million, property records show. Sunny Isles Beach, Fla.-based Optimar International Realty bought the retail condo, which is leased to a Casa Tua dining concept. It spans about 15,000 square feet at 2700 Northwest Second Avenue in Wynwood. Related Group and Tricap provided $26 million in seller financing. The joint venture completed the NoMad Residences this year, after buying the 1-acre site for $26.5 million in 2021 and securing a $142 million construction package in 2024. The nine-story building, branded after the now-shuttered New York hotel, houses 329 condos. (Hilton owns the NoMad brand.) The Casa Tua Cucina Italian food hall opened in April. Casa Tua, founded by husband-wife duo Miky and Leticia Grendene, counts another food hall at the Brickell City Center and an upscale restaurant in Miami Beach as part of the portfolio. The sale comes three months after New York-based TriCap sold the retail building leased to the popular Pastis French Bistro in Wynwood to Moishe Mana for $25 million, The Real Deal reported. In other retail deals in Wynwood, the owners of I Scream Gelato purchased its 1,325-square-foot parlor for about $3.7 million last year. Representatives for Related Group, Tricap and Optimar International Realty did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Group and Tricap sold NoMad Residences ground-floor retail condo in Miami Wynwood for $33M
15,000 sq ft retail leased to Casa Tua dining concept; $26M seller financing provided
9-story, 329-unit condo completed; 1-acre site acquired for $26.5M in 2021
stories.summary: Related Group and Tricap have sold the ground-floor retail space at NoMad Residences (their newly completed nine-story, 329-unit condo development in Miami's Wynwood) to Sunny Isles Beach-based Optimar International Realty for $33 million. The 15,000-square-foot retail space is leased to Casa Tua Cucina, an Italian food hall. The sponsors provided $26 million in seller financing and had secured $142 million in construction debt in 2024.
stories.impact: Retail-condo sale at high price point signals strong Miami investor appetite for mixed-use and hospitality-anchored properties. However, the condo structure and food-hall retail concept differ from pure multifamily development; developers should note tight multifamily supply in Wynwood and spillover demand into adjacent neighborhoods (Allapattah, Buena Vista). Monitor Class A rents and new construction feasibility; strong tourist/dining traffic may support premium rental rates and amenity-driven projects nearby.
